newsitem.title: TURKEY: Eleven dead in Turkish tourist bus crash.
newsitem.headline: Eleven dead in Turkish tourist bus crash.

text.p: A coach carrying German and Dutch holidaymakers plunged 30 metres (100 feet) down a ravine in southern Turkey on Thursday, killing 10 foreign tourists and a Turk, police and hospital officials said.
The accident happened in Korkuteli, near the popular resort city of Antalya.
"One Turkish citizen and 10 foreigners died in the crash," Alaadin Erdem, a doctor at Korkuteli hospital, told Reuters by telephone. Nineteen people were injured, he said.
The bus was carrying around 30 tourists, mostly German and Dutch, from Antalya to the inland town of Pamukkale. "It was bad weather, raining," a spokesman for the Dutch embassy said.
"I just spoke to one of the victims who was injured. One of her friends, a Dutch citizen, was killed," he said. "There are also Germans dead."
Turkey has one of the worst road traffic death rates in the world. Almost 6,000 people lost their lives in traffic accidents last year.
